title: Hybrid SPACE Hardness and whPRP Security
summary: Hybrid SPACE hardness lacks a proof-ready definition; it remains open to formalize the notion and determine whether it implies whPRP security for well-designed SPACE-hard block ciphers.

formal_statement.body: For well-designed SPACE-hard block ciphers, formalize hybrid SPACE hardness as a security notion suitable for security proofs and determine whether satisfying that notion implies $\mathrm{whPRP}$ security. Hybrid SPACE hardness is not currently a formal security definition usable in such proofs, although block ciphers satisfying it are expected to fulfill $\mathrm{whPRP}$.

scope.domain: Structural security notions connecting hybrid SPACE hardness and whPRP for well-designed SPACE-hard block ciphers.
assumptions: The block cipher satisfies hybrid SPACE hardness.
In the proposed simulator regime, the lifter-time bound is no greater than the simulator-query bound.
parameters: t_lif: time bound for the lifter
q_sim: query bound for the simulator
scope.unresolved_remainder: Formalize hybrid SPACE hardness for use in security proofs and determine whether it implies whPRP security.

citations.label: A Modular Approach to the Incompressibility of Block-Cipher-Based AEADs

progress.summary: The source presents the implication as an expectation rather than a proof because hybrid SPACE hardness is not yet a formal security definition. It supports the expectation with a heuristic table-search simulator when lifter time does not exceed the simulator-query bound.
